people.name: Guillaume Tirel
people.bio: French cook known as Taillevent. He rose from a kitchen boy to the chief cook of the royal kitchens, and the book Le Viandier carries his name.

milestones.event: Became chief cook of the kitchen of King Charles V.
Became squire of the kitchen of King Charles VI.

people.name: Michael Wolgemut
people.bio: Nuremberg painter whose workshop cut the woodcuts for large printed books.

milestones.event: Took the young Dürer as an apprentice.
His workshop supplied the woodcuts for the Nuremberg Chronicle.

people.name: Sandro Botticelli
people.bio: Italian painter of the early Renaissance in Florence.

milestones.event: Painted The Birth of Venus.

people.name: Leonardo da Vinci
people.bio: Italian painter, engineer and scientist of the High Renaissance.

milestones.event: Completed The Last Supper in Milan.
Started the Mona Lisa.

people.name: Albrecht Dürer
people.bio: German painter and printmaker who made the woodcut and the engraving into major art forms.

milestones.event: Published the Apocalypse, a set of sixteen woodcuts.
Engraved Melencolia I and St Jerome in His Study.

people.name: Raphael
people.bio: Italian painter of balanced High Renaissance compositions.

milestones.event: Completed The School of Athens in the Vatican.

people.name: Hieronymus Cock
people.bio: Antwerp publisher who split print work into design, engraving and sale.

milestones.event: Founded the print house Aux Quatre Vents in Antwerp.
Published his own last series, twelve landscape etchings.

people.name: Bartolomeo Scappi
people.bio: Italian cook of cardinals and popes. His Opera of 1570 holds about 1,000 recipes and shows the tools and the stations of a Renaissance kitchen.

milestones.event: Published the Opera dell'arte del cucinare in Venice.
Died in Rome.

people.name: Hendrick Goltzius
people.bio: Dutch engraver whose swelling lines set a standard for the engraved print.

milestones.event: Moved to Haarlem and engraved a Lucretia series for Philip Galle.
Travelled to Italy to study the art of Rome.

people.name: Caravaggio
people.bio: Italian painter whose strong light and dark changed European painting.

milestones.event: Completed The Calling of Saint Matthew in Rome.
Died on the way back to Rome.

people.name: Peter Paul Rubens
people.bio: Flemish painter of dynamic Baroque scenes.

milestones.event: Painted The Elevation of the Cross.

people.name: Jacques Callot
people.bio: Printmaker from Lorraine who made etching a precise medium with a hard ground and the échoppe needle.

photo.credit: Ignazio Enrico Hugford, after Antoon van Dyck (1599–1641), painter of the original

milestones.event: Started work in Florence for the Medici court.
Returned to Nancy and etched there for the rest of his life.

people.name: Rembrandt
people.bio: Dutch painter of light, shadow and portraits.

milestones.event: Made his first etchings.
Painted The Night Watch.

people.name: Ludwig von Siegen
people.bio: German soldier and amateur artist who made the first known mezzotint.

milestones.event: Finished the first known mezzotint, a portrait of Amalia Elisabeth, Landgravine of Hesse-Kassel.

people.name: Hishikawa Moronobu
people.bio: Japanese artist who made ukiyo-e into a form of single-sheet prints.

milestones.event: Signed his first illustrated books in Edo.

people.name: François Pierre de La Varenne
people.bio: French cook of the Marquis d'Uxelles. His book Le Cuisinier françois moved French cooking from heavy spice to stocks, roux and herbs.

milestones.event: Published Le Cuisinier françois.
Published Le Pastissier françois.

people.name: John Boydell
people.bio: London engraver and publisher who built an export trade in English prints.

milestones.event: Started his own engraving and print business in London.
Started the Shakespeare Gallery and its folio of engravings.

people.name: Madame de Pompadour
people.bio: Official mistress of Louis XV. She led French taste in dress, silk and porcelain, and she paid for the Rococo style.

milestones.event: Became the official mistress of Louis XV and took the title of marquise.
Died at Versailles.

people.name: Matthew Boulton
people.bio: English manufacturer in Birmingham. He ran the Soho Manufactory, where workers made buttons, buckles and small metal goods, among them cut steel ornaments, in large numbers.

milestones.event: Opened the Soho Manufactory at Birmingham, a factory for small metal goods.

people.name: Robert Adam
people.bio: Scottish architect who designed the room as one whole, from the ceiling plaster to the carpet, in a light neoclassical manner.

milestones.event: Returned to London from his Grand Tour of Italy and started his practice.
Published the first volume of The Works in Architecture of Robert and James Adam.
Published the first volume of The Works in Architecture, a source of classical models for makers of furniture, metalwork and ceramics.

people.name: Ann Lee
people.bio: English religious leader who founded the Shaker movement in America, whose way of life gave the Shaker style.

milestones.event: Sailed to America with a small group of followers.
Sailed to New York with 8 followers; the community that she led later made the plain Shaker furniture and boxes.

people.name: Abraham-Louis Breguet
people.bio: Swiss-born watchmaker in Paris. He made watches with a clear dial, a thin case and a steel hand, and he patented the tourbillon in 1801.

milestones.event: Opened his watch workshop in Paris.
Patented the tourbillon, a cage that turns the escapement to cancel the effect of gravity.

people.name: Rose Bertin
people.bio: French milliner and dressmaker. She supplied Queen Marie Antoinette and set the trimmed, ribboned gown of the late Rococo court.

milestones.event: Born at Abbeville, Picardy.
By this year she supplied Queen Marie Antoinette with gowns and hats, and the court called her the Minister of Fashion.

people.name: John Raphael Smith
people.bio: English mezzotint engraver who reproduced the portraits of Reynolds and others.

milestones.event: Moved to London to start a print business.
Issued his mezzotint of Mrs Carnac after Reynolds.

people.name: Marie Antoinette
people.bio: Queen of France from 1774 to 1792. The court of Versailles under her dressed in stays and wide gowns, and her dress set the rule for French court fashion.

milestones.event: Became queen of France; the court of Versailles wore boned stays under every formal gown.

people.name: Katsushika Hokusai
people.bio: Japanese ukiyo-e artist of landscapes and The Great Wave.

milestones.event: Published The Great Wave off Kanagawa in Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji.

people.name: Joséphine de Beauharnais
people.bio: Empress of the French from 1804. Her light muslin gowns and cashmere shawls set the fashion for the high-waisted dress.

milestones.event: Married Napoleon Bonaparte.
Crowned Empress at Notre-Dame; the court kept the high waist and the long, light line.

people.name: Beau Brummell
people.bio: English man of fashion at the court of the Prince Regent. He set the dark, plain, well-cut coat and the clean linen of the modern man's suit.

milestones.event: Took a commission in the 10th Light Dragoons, the Prince of Wales's regiment.
Fled to France to escape his debts, and left London dress to its tailors.

people.name: Marie-Antoine Carême
people.bio: French pastry cook and chef who worked for Talleyrand, the Prince Regent and the Rothschilds. He set the grand sauces in a system and built sugar and pastry monuments.

milestones.event: Published Le Pâtissier royal parisien and Le Pâtissier pittoresque.
Published Le Cuisinier parisien.
Died in Paris; his L'Art de la cuisine française was left unfinished.

people.name: Roxey Ann Caplin
people.bio: English corsetmaker and author. She argued for corsets that fit the body, wrote on dress and health, and filed many patents for corsets and crinolines.

milestones.event: Worked as a corsetmaker at 58 Berners Street, London.
Won a medal for her corsets at the Great Exhibition.
Held 24 patents by this year.

people.name: Utagawa Hiroshige
people.bio: Japanese ukiyo-e artist of travel landscapes.

milestones.event: Published The Fifty-three Stations of the Tōkaidō.
Started One Hundred Famous Views of Edo.

people.name: Darius Wells
people.bio: American printer who cut wood type by machine and made it cheap enough for posters.

milestones.event: Published his first known wood-type catalogue in New York.

people.name: Henry Cole
people.bio: English civil servant and design reformer who organised the Great Exhibition of 1851 and founded the museum that became the Victoria and Albert Museum.

milestones.event: Began to sell household goods by good artists, as Summerly's Art Manufactures.
Helped to organise the Great Exhibition, which showed the goods of the machine age to 6 million visitors.

people.name: Aaron Lufkin Dennison
people.bio: American watchmaker who set up the first American factory for machine-made watches with interchangeable parts. His firm became the Waltham Watch Company.

milestones.event: Founded the Boston Watch Company with Howard and Davis; the firm later became the Waltham Watch Company.

people.name: Julia Margaret Cameron
nationality: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland
people.bio: British photographer of soft-focus portraits in the 1860s.

milestones.event: Started to take photographs.

people.name: Queen Victoria
people.bio: British queen from 1837. Her court and her household set the manner of dress, and her elastic-sided boots made the style respectable.

milestones.event: Opened the Great Exhibition in London, where bootmakers showed their boots to a mass public.
Mourned Prince Albert, who died in December, and wore black mourning jewellery for many years; jet became the fashion.

people.name: Louis Vuitton
people.bio: French trunk-maker. He opened his shop in Paris in 1854 and sold a flat-topped trunk in grey coated canvas that stacked and shed rain.

milestones.event: Opened his trunk-maker's shop in Paris and sold the flat-topped trunk in coated canvas.
Opened a workshop at Asnières, near Paris.
Added a striped canvas, the first pattern on his trunks.

people.name: Charles Frederick Worth
people.bio: English couturier in Paris. He founded the first modern fashion house and dressed the Second Empire court in the cage crinoline and then the bustle.

milestones.event: Opened the House of Worth at 7 rue de la Paix, Paris, with Otto Bobergh.
Became the dressmaker of Empress Eugénie after Princess Pauline de Metternich presented him.

people.name: Levi Strauss
people.bio: German-born merchant of San Francisco. He backed the patent of Jacob Davis and made the riveted waist overall in his own factory.

milestones.event: Moved to San Francisco and opened a dry goods house.
Made the riveted waist overall under the patent that he shared with Jacob Davis.

people.name: Camille Pissarro
people.bio: Danish-French painter, the only one who showed at all eight Impressionist exhibitions.

milestones.event: Showed at the first Impressionist exhibition.

people.name: Jacob Davis
people.bio: Tailor of Reno, Nevada. He set copper rivets at the stress points of work trousers and, with Levi Strauss, took a patent for the idea in 1873.

milestones.event: Took US patent 139,121 with Levi Strauss for work trousers with riveted pockets.

people.name: Charles Goodyear Jr.
people.bio: American inventor and son of the rubber pioneer. He built the machine that sews a welt to the upper, which became the basis of the dress shoe trade.

milestones.event: Built a machine that sews a welt to the upper and the insole; the Goodyear welt takes its name from it.

people.name: William Morris
nationality: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland
people.bio: English designer, writer and socialist who made the handmade room a political idea and founded the Arts and Crafts movement.

milestones.event: Moved into the Red House, designed with Philip Webb and furnished by hand.
Founded the decorating firm Morris, Marshall, Faulkner and Co.
Morris, Marshall, Faulkner and Co. sold the adjustable Morris chair and the Sussex chair, c. 1865–66, made in small workshops with plain oak and rush.
Took sole control of the firm, renamed Morris and Co.
Founded the Kelmscott Press.

people.name: Thomas Burberry
people.bio: English outfitter. He opened a shop at Basingstoke in 1856 and made gabardine in 1879, the cloth of the trench coat.

milestones.event: Opened an outfitter's shop at Basingstoke.
Made gabardine, a rain cloth woven from proofed yarn.
His firm adapted the army officer's raincoat for the war, and the coat became the trench coat.

people.name: Charles Eastlake
nationality: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland
people.bio: English architect and writer whose advice book on household taste gave a simpler line to the late Victorian room.

milestones.event: Published Hints on Household Taste.

people.name: Jules Chéret
people.bio: French lithographer who made the colour poster a street art.

milestones.event: Started a period of lithography training in London.
Sold his lithography company to Imprimerie Chaix and became its artistic director.

people.name: Caroline Reboux
people.bio: French milliner who ran one of the best-known hat houses of Paris from 1865, in the years when the poke bonnet gave way to the small hat.

milestones.event: Opened her millinery house in the rue de la Paix, Paris.

people.name: Benjamin Day Jr.
people.bio: American illustrator who invented the Ben Day dot process for tone and colour.

milestones.event: Developed the Ben Day process of dot patterns.

people.name: Claude Monet
people.bio: French painter whose picture gave Impressionism its name.

milestones.event: Painted Impression, Sunrise.
Showed at the first Impressionist exhibition.
Started his Water Lilies paintings.

people.name: T. J. Cobden-Sanderson
nationality: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland
people.bio: English bookbinder and printer who ran the Doves Press.

milestones.event: Set up the Doves Bindery in Hammersmith.
Started to throw the Doves Type into the Thames (1913 is the traditional date; his journals give 1916–17).

people.name: Berthe Morisot
people.bio: French painter, a founding member of the Impressionist group.

milestones.event: Showed at the first Impressionist exhibition.

people.name: Karl Benz
people.bio: German engineer. His three-wheeled Patent-Motorwagen of 1886 is the first car that was built as one machine, not as a carriage with an engine.

milestones.event: Founded Benz & Cie in Mannheim.
Received the patent for the Patent-Motorwagen.
Sold the Velo, the first car made in series.

people.name: Auguste Escoffier
people.bio: French chef who ran the kitchens of the Savoy, the Ritz and the Carlton with César Ritz, organised the brigade de cuisine and wrote Le Guide culinaire.

milestones.event: Took charge of the kitchen of the Savoy Hotel in London.
Created the pêche Melba for Nellie Melba.
Published Le Guide culinaire.

people.name: Webb C. Ball
people.bio: American jeweller of Cleveland who set the rules for railroad watches. His standard fixed the accuracy and the marking of a watch that a train crew could use.

milestones.event: Became chief time inspector for railroads and set strict watch standards.

people.name: César Ritz
people.bio: Swiss hotelier who managed the Savoy and founded the Ritz in Paris; he gave Escoffier the grand hotel kitchen and its dining room.

milestones.event: Became manager of the Savoy Hotel in London, with Escoffier as chef.
Opened the Hôtel Ritz in Paris.

people.name: Emery Walker
people.bio: English engraver and typographer who advised William Morris and co-founded the Doves Press.

milestones.event: Became a partner in the Doves Press and supervised the Doves Type.
Received a knighthood.

people.name: Antoni Gaudí
people.bio: Catalan architect of Modernisme, the Barcelona form of Art Nouveau, with curved stone and mosaic.

milestones.event: Took over the Sagrada Família project in Barcelona.
Completed the Casa Batlló in Barcelona.

people.name: Gertrude Käsebier
people.bio: American photographer of soft-focus portraits and a founder of the Photo-Secession.

milestones.event: Co-founded the Photo-Secession.

people.name: Inès Gaches-Sarraute
people.bio: French physician and corsetmaker. Alarmed by the effect of tight corsets on the body, she designed a health corset with a straight front, later called the S-bend corset.

milestones.event: Introduced her health corset, later called the S-bend corset, in a book on the corset.

people.name: Erik Werenskiold
people.bio: Norwegian painter and illustrator of Norwegian folk tales.

milestones.event: Started to illustrate the folk tales of Asbjørnsen and Moe.

people.name: Theodor Kittelsen
people.bio: Norwegian painter of trolls and the Norwegian landscape.

milestones.event: Published the plague drawings Svartedauen.

people.name: Alphonse Mucha
people.bio: Czech artist whose posters of women in flowing lines became the image of Art Nouveau.

milestones.event: Made the poster Gismonda for Sarah Bernhardt.
Started The Slav Epic.

people.name: René Lalique
people.bio: French jeweller and glass maker. He used horn, enamel and opal as well as gems, and he drew the curved, natural forms of Art Nouveau jewels.

milestones.event: Showed his jewels at the Exposition Universelle in Paris.

people.name: Fridtjof Nansen
people.bio: Norwegian explorer and scientist. His ski and sledge journeys in wool and windproof dress gave a model to the Nordic life of the open air.

milestones.event: Crossed Greenland on skis with a party of five.
Sailed on the Fram towards the North Pole.

people.name: Victor Horta
people.bio: Belgian architect who made the first Art Nouveau houses, with iron and glass that follow the line of a plant.

milestones.event: Completed the Hôtel Tassel in Brussels, the first Art Nouveau house.
Completed the Hôtel Solvay in Brussels, with the furniture, the door handles and the lamps of his own design.
Completed the Maison du Peuple in Brussels.

people.name: Charles Robert Ashbee
people.bio: English architect and designer. He founded the Guild of Handicraft and drew silver and enamel jewels that the guild made by hand.

milestones.event: Founded the Guild of Handicraft in London.

people.name: Alfred Stieglitz
people.bio: American photographer and gallerist who led Pictorialism and then turned against it.

milestones.event: Founded the Photo-Secession.
Took The Steerage.
Published Paul Strand's work in the last issue of Camera Work.

people.name: Akseli Gallen-Kallela
people.bio: Finnish painter of the Kalevala epic.

milestones.event: Painted The Defence of the Sampo.
Painted frescoes for the Finnish pavilion at the Paris World Fair.

people.name: Hector Guimard
people.bio: French architect who gave Paris its Art Nouveau metro entrances.

milestones.event: Completed the Castel Béranger in Paris.
Designed the cast-iron railings, door handles and stoves of the Castel Béranger.
Designed the first entrances of the Paris Métro.

people.name: Piet Mondrian
people.bio: Dutch painter of grids of black lines and primary colours.

milestones.event: Co-founded De Stijl.
Painted his first compositions in red, yellow, blue and black.
Painted Broadway Boogie Woogie in New York.

people.name: Alberto Santos-Dumont
people.bio: Brazilian aviator in Paris. By the account of the Cartier house, he asked for a watch that he could read in flight without a hand on a pocket chain.

milestones.event: By the account of the Cartier house, asked Louis Cartier for a watch to wear on the wrist in flight.

people.name: Robert Wiene
people.bio: German film director of The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari.

milestones.event: Released The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari.

people.name: Louis Cartier
people.bio: French jeweller who ran the house of Cartier. He made the wristwatch a gentleman's piece with the Santos and the Tank.

milestones.event: Moved the family house to the rue de la Paix in Paris, where it made garland-style jewels in platinum.
By the account of the Cartier house, made a wristwatch for the aviator Alberto Santos-Dumont.
Drew the Tank, a rectangular watch with straight lugs that follow the lines of the case.

people.name: August Sander
people.bio: German portrait photographer who recorded the people of his country by trade and class in a frontal, plain manner.

milestones.event: Published the portrait book Antlitz der Zeit.

people.name: Madeleine Vionnet
people.bio: French couturière. She drew her gowns on a small wooden doll and made the bias cut the base of the draped dress of the 1930s.

milestones.event: Opened her own house in Paris.
Closed her house at the start of the war.

people.name: Edward Steichen
people.bio: Luxembourg-American photographer who moved from Pictorialism to modern fashion photography.

milestones.event: Took The Pond—Moonlight.
Curated The Family of Man at MoMA.

people.name: Émile-Jacques Ruhlmann
people.bio: French furniture maker and decorator whose veneered, ivory-inlaid rooms set the standard of Art Deco luxury.

milestones.event: Founded the firm Ruhlmann et Laurent in Paris.
Showed the Hôtel du Collectionneur pavilion at the Paris exposition of decorative arts.
Furnished the Hôtel du Collectionneur with cabinets, chairs and lamps in ebony and ivory.

people.name: Pablo Picasso
people.bio: Spanish painter who started Cubism with Georges Braque.

milestones.event: Painted Les Demoiselles d'Avignon.
Painted Guernica.

people.name: Raymond Hood
people.bio: American architect of Art Deco skyscrapers in New York.

milestones.event: Completed the American Radiator Building in New York.
Completed 30 Rockefeller Plaza as lead architect.

people.name: George Barbier
people.bio: French illustrator whose fashion plates were coloured by hand through stencils.

milestones.event: Started to write and draw for the Gazette du Bon Ton.
Published the almanac Falbalas et Fanfreluches.

people.name: Georges Braque
people.bio: French painter who started Cubism with Pablo Picasso.

milestones.event: Painted Houses at L'Estaque.
Made the first papier collé.

people.name: Gabrielle Chanel
people.bio: French couturière. She put jersey, the straight chemise and the short skirt into couture, made costume jewellery a fashion, and in 1955 launched the quilted flap bag on a chain.

milestones.event: Opened a hat shop in Paris.
Showed day dresses in jersey, a cloth that men used for underwear.
Wore long ropes of imitation pearls and large false jewels with her day clothes, and made them the fashion.
Showed a short black crêpe dress that American Vogue compared to the Ford car.
Launched the quilted bag with a chain strap, named for its month and year.

people.name: Theo van Doesburg
people.bio: Dutch artist who founded the magazine De Stijl and spread its ideas across Europe.

milestones.event: Founded the magazine De Stijl.
Started Elementarism and added the diagonal.

people.name: Walter Gropius
people.bio: German architect who founded the Bauhaus school and later taught modern architecture at Harvard.

milestones.event: Founded the Bauhaus in Weimar.
Completed the Bauhaus building in Dessau.
Started to teach at the Harvard Graduate School of Design.

people.name: William Van Alen
people.bio: American architect of the Chrysler Building, the tallest Art Deco tower of its day.

milestones.event: Completed the Chrysler Building in New York.
Wore a costume of his building at the Beaux-Arts Ball in New York.

people.name: Edward Weston
people.bio: American photographer of sharp still lifes and landscapes, a founder of Group f/64.

milestones.event: Took Pepper No. 30.
Co-founded Group f/64.

people.name: George Mallory
people.bio: English mountaineer. He went to Everest in 1921, 1922 and 1924, and died on the mountain in layers of wool and silk under a gabardine smock.

milestones.event: Went to Everest with the first reconnaissance party.
Took part in the second Everest expedition.
Died near the summit of Everest in layers of wool, silk and gabardine.

people.name: Ludwig Mies van der Rohe
people.bio: German-American architect of steel and glass, and the last director of the Bauhaus.

milestones.event: Completed the Barcelona Pavilion.
Became director of the Bauhaus.
Completed the Seagram Building in New York.

people.name: Le Corbusier
people.bio: Swiss-French architect who wrote the five points of a new architecture and used raw concrete in his late work.

milestones.event: Published Vers une architecture.
Completed the Villa Savoye in Poissy.
Completed the Unité d'Habitation in Marseille, in béton brut.

people.name: F. W. Murnau
people.bio: German film director of Nosferatu.

milestones.event: Released Nosferatu.
Released The Last Laugh.

people.name: Paul Jaray
people.bio: Engineer born in Vienna. He worked on airship hulls and then used wind-tunnel tests to shape the body of a car.

milestones.event: Joined the Zeppelin airship works in Friedrichshafen.
Patented a streamlined car body.

people.name: P. V. H. Weems
people.bio: American naval officer and navigation teacher. He designed the Hour Angle watch for pilots with the help of Charles Lindbergh.

milestones.event: Designed the Hour Angle watch for long-distance navigation, made by Longines.

people.name: El Lissitzky
people.bio: Russian artist and designer of Constructivist books and exhibitions.

milestones.event: Made the poster Beat the Whites with the Red Wedge.
Designed the book For the Voice.

people.name: Fritz Lang
people.bio: Austrian-German film director of Metropolis and M.

milestones.event: Released the film Metropolis.
Released the film M.

people.name: Paul Strand
people.bio: American photographer whose sharp, direct pictures defined straight photography.

milestones.event: Took Blind Woman in New York.
His work filled the last issue of Camera Work.

people.name: Alexander Rodchenko
people.bio: Russian artist who made Constructivist posters, photographs and typography.

milestones.event: Signed the Constructivist programme and left easel painting.
Made the Books poster with Lilya Brik.

people.name: Caresse Crosby
people.bio: American socialite and publisher, born Mary Phelps Jacob. She patented the backless brassière, a light band of two handkerchiefs and ribbon that did not need a corset.

milestones.event: Filed a patent for the backless brassière on 12 February.
Received the first US patent in the new class of brassières on 3 November, and later sold the patent to the Warner Brothers Corset Company.

people.name: Raymond Templier
people.bio: French jeweller of a Paris family firm. He drew hard, geometric jewels in platinum, diamond and black onyx.

milestones.event: Showed geometric jewels at the Exposition des Arts Décoratifs in Paris.

people.name: Richard Neutra
people.bio: Austrian-American architect of glass houses in the California landscape.

milestones.event: Completed the Lovell Health House in Los Angeles.
Completed the Kaufmann Desert House in Palm Springs.

people.name: Battista Pininfarina
people.bio: Italian coachbuilder. He founded his Turin workshop in 1930 and made clean, low car bodies that became the model of the grand tourer.

milestones.event: Founded the Carrozzeria Pinin Farina in Turin.
Built the Cisitalia 202 coupe, with the wings joined into the body.
The Museum of Modern Art in New York showed the Cisitalia 202.

people.name: Harley Earl
people.bio: American designer. He led styling at General Motors from 1927, and he added the tail fin, the wrap-around glass and the dream car to the car trade.

milestones.event: Started the Art and Colour Section at General Motors.
Put the first tail fins on a Cadillac.
Opened the Motorama show of dream cars.

people.name: Marianne Brandt
people.bio: German designer of Bauhaus metal objects and lamps.

milestones.event: Designed the MT49 tea infuser.
Became head of the Bauhaus metal workshop.

people.name: Raymond Loewy
people.bio: French-born American industrial designer who gave trains, refrigerators and small appliances a smooth, rounded shell.

milestones.event: Drew a streamlined pencil sharpener to show that a small object can carry a teardrop shell.
Redesigned the Coldspot refrigerator with a rounded body and a flush door.

people.name: Edward VIII
people.bio: King of the United Kingdom in 1936. As Prince of Wales he set the model of men's country dress: Fair Isle jumpers, plus-fours and strong tweed checks.

milestones.event: Wore a Fair Isle jumper to play golf, and the knit became a fashion.

people.name: Dorothea Lange
people.bio: American photographer whose pictures of farm workers and migrants in the 1930s made the case for relief.

milestones.event: Took Migrant Mother for the Resettlement Administration.

people.name: Jean Saudé
people.bio: French printmaker in Paris who ran a pochoir workshop and wrote the guide to the method.

milestones.event: Published the guide Traité d'enluminure d'art au pochoir.

people.name: László Moholy-Nagy
people.bio: Hungarian artist and teacher who brought photography and typography into the Bauhaus.

milestones.event: Started to teach the preliminary course at the Bauhaus.
Founded the New Bauhaus in Chicago.

people.name: Dziga Vertov
people.bio: Soviet documentary director of the Kino-Eye.

milestones.event: Released Man with a Movie Camera.

people.name: Wallace Carothers
people.bio: American chemist who led organic chemistry research at DuPont and is credited with the invention of nylon, the fibre of the stocking and the girdle.

milestones.event: Led the DuPont team that made the first nylon polymer.

people.name: Warren Marrison
people.bio: Canadian-born American engineer at Bell Telephone Laboratories. In 1927 he built the first quartz clock, the root of the quartz watch.

milestones.event: Built the first quartz clock at Bell Telephone Laboratories.

people.name: Fernand Point
people.bio: French restaurateur and cook of La Pyramide in Vienne. He trained many chefs of the next generation, among them Paul Bocuse, the Troisgros brothers and Alain Chapel.

milestones.event: Took over his father's restaurant in Vienne and named it La Pyramide.
La Pyramide won three Michelin stars.
Died in Vienne.

people.name: Alvar Aalto
people.bio: Finnish architect and designer of bent plywood furniture.

milestones.event: Designed the Paimio armchair of bent birch plywood.
Completed the Paimio Sanatorium and its Paimio chair.
Founded Artek.

people.name: Fulco di Verdura
people.bio: Sicilian duke and jewel designer. He drew gold and gem jewels for Chanel, and then made warm, sculpted clips and cuffs with large stones.

milestones.event: Opened his own jewellery house in New York.

people.name: Salvatore Ferragamo
people.bio: Italian shoemaker. He made shoes for film and stage in California, then in Florence, and he tried many new lasts, heels and soles.

milestones.event: Opened a shop in Hollywood and made custom shoes for film dancers and stars.
Made the Rainbow sandal with a raised, covered wedge sole, a forerunner of the platform shoe.

people.name: Sergei Eisenstein
people.bio: Soviet film director and theorist of montage.

milestones.event: Released Battleship Potemkin.
Released October.

people.name: Eddie Bauer
people.bio: American outdoorsman. He opened a sports shop in Seattle in 1920 and in 1936 made the first quilted down jacket.

milestones.event: Opened a sporting goods shop in Seattle.
Made the first quilted jacket with box baffles of goose down.
Made down flight parkas for the US Army Air Forces.

people.name: Lev Kuleshov
people.bio: Soviet film theorist who showed that a cut makes meaning.

milestones.event: Founded his workshop at the Moscow Film School.
Made the editing experiment now called the Kuleshov effect.

people.name: Herbert Bayer
people.bio: Austrian-American designer who made the Bauhaus typography and its single-case alphabet.

milestones.event: Designed the Universal alphabet at the Bauhaus.
Moved to the United States and curated the Bauhaus show at MoMA.

people.name: William Haines
people.bio: American film actor who became the decorator of the Hollywood stars and gave Regency forms a glamorous film-set finish.

milestones.event: Completed the interiors of Sunnylands, the Annenberg estate in Rancho Mirage.

people.name: A. M. Cassandre
people.bio: French poster artist and type designer of the Art Deco period.

milestones.event: Made the Étoile du Nord railway poster.
Made the Normandie liner poster.

people.name: Chuck Taylor
people.bio: American basketball player and salesman. He taught the game with the canvas shoe and gave it his name.

milestones.event: His name went on the ankle patch of the canvas basketball shoe, which sold under it for decades.

people.name: Jean Prouvé
people.bio: French metalworker, designer and engineer who made furniture and lamps of bent and welded steel for schools, offices and factories.

milestones.event: Designed the Standard chair of pressed and welded steel.
Designed the Potence wall lamp with a swivel arm of steel tube.

people.name: Ansel Adams
people.bio: American photographer of the American West and inventor of the Zone System.

milestones.event: Co-founded Group f/64.
Took Moonrise, Hernandez, New Mexico.

people.name: Arne Jacobsen
people.bio: Danish architect and designer of the Ant, Egg and Swan chairs.

milestones.event: Designed the Ant chair.
Completed the SAS Royal Hotel in Copenhagen.

people.name: Charles Lindbergh
people.bio: American aviator who flew solo across the Atlantic in 1927. He took part in the design of a watch that a pilot could use to find the longitude.

milestones.event: Took part in the design of the Hour Angle watch with P. V. H. Weems.

people.name: Marcel Breuer
people.bio: Hungarian-American architect and furniture designer of tubular steel chairs.

milestones.event: Designed the Wassily chair.
Completed the Whitney Museum building in New York.

people.name: Charles Arpels
people.bio: French jeweller of the house Van Cleef & Arpels. In 1933 his firm registered the minaudière, a rigid evening case with compartments.

milestones.event: Registered the minaudière, a rigid evening case with compartments, at Van Cleef & Arpels.

people.name: Margaret De Patta
people.bio: American jeweller and teacher. She made small abstract jewels by hand from silver and cut stones, with ideas from modern art.

milestones.event: Studied under László Moholy-Nagy in Chicago, and then made abstract jewels at the bench.

people.name: Mark Rothko
people.bio: American painter of large soft fields of colour.

milestones.event: Painted his first colour-field works.
The Rothko Chapel opened in Houston.

people.name: Arthur Kneibler
people.bio: American designer at Coopers, Inc. of Kenosha. He designed the first Y-front brief, with a short leg, an elastic waist and an overlapping Y-shaped fly.

milestones.event: Designed the Y-front brief for Coopers, Inc.
Saw the first briefs go on sale at a store in Chicago on 19 January; the shop sold over 30,000 pairs in three months.

people.name: Isamu Noguchi
people.bio: Japanese-American sculptor and designer who joined Japanese craft and modern design.

milestones.event: Designed the Noguchi table for Herman Miller.
Designed the first Akari paper lamps.
Joined Japanese paper and bamboo craft to modern form in the first Akari lamps.

people.name: Willem de Kooning
people.bio: Dutch-American painter of violent gestural brushwork.

milestones.event: Painted Excavation.
Painted Woman I.

people.name: Christian Dior
people.bio: French couturier. His first collection, in 1947, set the small waist and the full skirt of post-war dress.

milestones.event: Opened his couture house at 30 avenue Montaigne, Paris.
Showed the Corolle line with the Bar suit; Carmel Snow called it the New Look.
Showed the H-line, a straight line with a low waist.

people.name: Philip Johnson
people.bio: American architect and curator who named the International Style and later turned to Postmodernism.

milestones.event: Curated the Modern Architecture show at MoMA, which named the International Style.
Completed the Glass House in New Canaan.
Completed the AT&T Building in New York, with a broken pediment on top.

people.name: Altina Schinasi
people.bio: American designer and artist. She drew the Harlequin glasses, the first cat-eye frame, in 1939 and sold them in New York shops.

milestones.event: Designed the Harlequin frame, with raised outer corners, and sold it in New York shops.

people.name: Charles Eames
people.bio: American designer who, with Ray Eames, made moulded plywood and plastic furniture.

milestones.event: Put the moulded plywood chair into production with Ray Eames.
Completed the Eames House in Los Angeles with Ray Eames.
Designed the Eames Lounge Chair with Ray Eames.

people.name: Roger Vivier
people.bio: French shoe designer. He worked for the couture houses and shaped the thin heel and the pointed court shoe of the 1950s.

milestones.event: Opened his own shoe house in Paris.
Began to make the shoes for the Dior collections, with thin, steel-cored heels.

people.name: George Nelson
people.bio: American designer and design director of Herman Miller.

milestones.event: Became design director of Herman Miller.
Designed the Ball Clock.

people.name: Henri Cartier-Bresson
people.bio: French photographer of the decisive moment and a founder of Magnum.

milestones.event: Co-founded Magnum Photos.
Published Images à la sauvette (The Decisive Moment).

people.name: Nicholas Kurti
people.bio: Hungarian-born physicist of Oxford, who argued that cooks should study the physics of food, and who founded the field of molecular gastronomy with Hervé This.

milestones.event: Gave the lecture The Physicist in the Kitchen at the Royal Institution in London.
Co-founded the workshop on molecular and physical gastronomy in Erice with Hervé This.

people.name: Jean Bugatti
people.bio: Son of Ettore Bugatti. He drew the bodies of the Type 57 cars, with a sharp seam along the top of each wing.

milestones.event: Drew the Type 57 Ventoux and Atalante bodies.
Showed the Type 57S Atlantic, with a riveted spine along the roof.

people.name: Eero Saarinen
people.bio: Finnish-American architect and furniture designer of sweeping concrete roofs and the Tulip chair.

milestones.event: Designed the Tulip chair for Knoll.
Completed the TWA Flight Center in New York.

people.name: Julius Shulman
people.bio: American photographer whose pictures of modernist houses in California set the way that architecture is shown.

milestones.event: Photographed the Kaufmann House in Palm Springs by Richard Neutra.
Took Case Study House #22, the Stahl House.

people.name: Max Miedinger
people.bio: Swiss type designer who drew Neue Haas Grotesk, later Helvetica.

milestones.event: Drew Neue Haas Grotesk with Eduard Hoffmann.
Neue Haas Grotesk was renamed Helvetica.

people.name: Bill Bowerman
people.bio: American athletics coach at the University of Oregon. He made shoes for his runners by hand and co-founded the company that became Nike.

milestones.event: Co-founded Blue Ribbon Sports to sell running shoes.
Poured rubber into a waffle iron to make a light, grippy sole.

people.name: Jackson Pollock
people.bio: American painter who poured and dripped paint on canvas laid on the floor.

milestones.event: Started his drip paintings.
Painted Autumn Rhythm.

people.name: Ray Eames
people.bio: American artist and designer who, with Charles Eames, made modern furniture and films.

milestones.event: Completed the Eames House in Los Angeles with Charles Eames.
Released the film Powers of Ten with Charles Eames.

people.name: Wilbert L. Gore
people.bio: American engineer. He left a chemical firm in 1958 and founded W. L. Gore and Associates at Newark, Delaware, the firm that made the Gore-Tex membrane.

milestones.event: Founded his firm at Newark, Delaware.
His son Bob stretched a rod of PTFE and made the porous membrane that the firm later sold in Gore-Tex.
His firm sold the first membrane cloth for garments.

people.name: Hans Wegner
people.bio: Danish furniture designer of the Wishbone chair.

milestones.event: Designed The Chair.
Designed the Wishbone chair for Carl Hansen & Søn.
Designed the Wishbone chair of steam-bent ash and a paper cord seat.

people.name: Josef Müller-Brockmann
people.bio: Swiss graphic designer of grid systems and concert posters.

milestones.event: Made the Der Film poster.
Published Grid Systems in Graphic Design.

people.name: Paul Rand
people.bio: American graphic designer of corporate logos and playful modern layouts.

milestones.event: Designed the IBM logo.
Designed the Westinghouse logo.

people.name: Klaus Märtens
people.bio: German army doctor. He injured his ankle in 1945 and designed a boot with an air-cushioned sole, the sole of the later workboot.

milestones.event: Injured his ankle skiing and designed boots with air-cushioned soles.
Founded a company at Seeshaupt, Germany, on the sole patent.

people.name: Noboru Hayama
people.bio: Japanese founder of Riso Kagaku, the maker of the Risograph and Print Gocco.

milestones.event: Founded Riso Kagaku in Tokyo.
His company started to sell the Print Gocco kit.

people.name: Ettore Sottsass
people.bio: Italian architect and designer who founded the Memphis Group.

milestones.event: Designed the red Valentine typewriter for Olivetti.
Designed the Carlton bookcase.
Founded the Memphis Group in Milan.
Drew the Carlton bookcase for the first Memphis collection.

people.name: Irving Penn
people.bio: American photographer known for clean studio fashion work, still lifes and portraits in a plain corner.

milestones.event: Made his first cover for Vogue.
Photographed the Harlequin Dress for Rochas.

people.name: John F. Kennedy
people.bio: 35th President of the United States and a Harvard man. His natural-shouldered suits and easy dress made the Ivy look a national style.

milestones.event: Graduated from Harvard College.
Took office as President; his suits and bare head set the Ivy look in the news.

people.name: Corita Kent
people.bio: American nun, teacher and artist who made screen prints of words and bright colour.

milestones.event: Started to teach art at Immaculate Heart College.
Became chair of the college art department.

people.name: Armin Hofmann
people.bio: Swiss graphic designer and teacher at the Basel School of Design.

milestones.event: Published Graphic Design Manual.

people.name: Saul Bass
people.bio: American graphic designer of film titles and posters in cut-paper shapes.

milestones.event: Designed the titles of The Man with the Golden Arm.
Designed the titles of Vertigo.

people.name: Andrew Grima
people.bio: Anglo-Italian jewellery designer in London. He made heavy jewels of textured gold with rough and uncut stones.

milestones.event: Showed textured gold jewels with uncut stones from his London house.

people.name: Pierre Cardin
people.bio: Italian-born French couturier. His 1960s collections of geometric tunics, tubes and helmets gave space-age dress its shapes.

milestones.event: Showed a space-age collection of geometric tunics, tubes and helmet hats.

people.name: Rudi Gernreich
people.bio: Austrian-born American designer. He made light, unlined clothes that follow the body, and he showed a bra without bone, pad or seam in 1964.

milestones.event: Showed the No Bra, a soft, sheer bra without bone or lining, made with a maker of foundation garments.

people.name: André Courrèges
people.bio: French couturier. His 1964 Space Age collection set the short white A-line dress, the flat trouser and the low boot as the look of the space age.

milestones.event: Opened his own couture house in Paris, after years in the atelier of Balenciaga.
Showed the Space Age collection: white A-line mini dresses, flat trousers and low boots.

people.name: Bob Maloubier
people.bio: French naval commando and diving pioneer. With Claude Riffaud he drew the diving watch that Blancpain made as the Fifty Fathoms.

milestones.event: Drew the specification for a diver's watch with Claude Riffaud; Blancpain made it as the Fifty Fathoms.

people.name: Peter Smithson
nationality: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland
people.bio: English architect who, with Alison Smithson, started the New Brutalism.

milestones.event: Completed Hunstanton School, the first New Brutalist building.
Completed Robin Hood Gardens in London.

people.name: Richard Avedon
people.bio: American photographer who made fashion pictures full of motion and portraits against a plain white ground.

milestones.event: Took Dovima with Elephants in Paris.

people.name: Roy Lichtenstein
people.bio: American Pop artist who painted comic panels with Ben-Day dots.

milestones.event: Painted Look Mickey.
Painted Whaam!.

people.name: Lee Iacocca
people.bio: American car executive. He led the Mustang project at Ford, a short, low, cheap car with a long list of options.

milestones.event: Joined Ford as an engineer.
Launched the Mustang at the New York World's Fair.

people.name: Robert Venturi
people.bio: American architect who argued for complexity and contradiction against the purity of Modernism.

photo.credit: todd sheridan from New York, United States

milestones.event: Completed the Vanna Venturi House in Philadelphia.
Published Complexity and Contradiction in Architecture.
Published Learning from Las Vegas with Denise Scott Brown and Steven Izenour.

people.name: Paul Bocuse
people.bio: French chef of Collonges-au-Mont-d'Or near Lyon. He made the Auberge du Pont de Collonges a three-star restaurant, cooked from the market and made the chef a public figure. He started the Bocuse d'Or in 1987.

milestones.event: The Auberge du Pont de Collonges won its third Michelin star.
Created the black truffle soup for a dinner at the Élysée Palace.

people.name: Verner Panton
people.bio: Danish furniture and lighting designer of bright, curved and one-piece plastic objects.

milestones.event: Drew the Panton chair, a cantilever seat in one shell.
Saw the Panton chair go into series production in moulded plastic.

people.name: Vivian Maier
people.bio: American street photographer whose work was found after her death.

milestones.event: Her negatives were bought at an auction in Chicago.

people.name: Thea Porter
people.bio: British designer, born in Jerusalem. Her long printed dresses and caftans of Middle Eastern cloth made her a maker of hippie and bohemian dress in London.

milestones.event: Sold caftans and long dresses of Middle Eastern cloth from her Soho shop in London.

people.name: Adrian Frutiger
people.bio: Swiss type designer whose Frutiger typeface, the humanist sans of airports and system interfaces, gave Frutiger Aero its name.

milestones.event: Released the Univers typeface.
Released the Frutiger typeface.

people.name: Agnès Varda
people.bio: Belgian-born French film director whose first film came before the New Wave.

milestones.event: Released La Pointe Courte.
Released Cléo from 5 to 7.

people.name: Alison Smithson
people.bio: English architect who, with Peter Smithson, started the New Brutalism.

milestones.event: Completed Hunstanton School with Peter Smithson.
Completed Robin Hood Gardens in London.

people.name: Andy Warhol
people.bio: American artist who used silkscreen and commercial images in Pop Art.

milestones.event: Showed Campbell's Soup Cans in Los Angeles.
Started to make silkscreen paintings and prints.
Opened the Factory studio in New York.

people.name: Christian Millau
people.bio: French food critic and writer. With Henri Gault he wrote the Gault Millau guide, which gave the new light kitchen of the 1970s a name and a list of rules.

milestones.event: Started Le Nouveau Guide with Henri Gault.
Published with Gault the ten characteristics of nouvelle cuisine.

people.name: Donald Judd
people.bio: American artist who turned a cast-iron factory building in SoHo into a home and studio and kept its open floors and large windows.

milestones.event: Bought 101 Spring Street, a five-storey cast-iron building in SoHo, New York.
Started to move his work and home to Marfa, Texas.

people.name: Garry Winogrand
people.bio: American street photographer of New York in the 1960s.

milestones.event: Showed in the New Documents exhibition at MoMA.

people.name: Nicolas Hayek
people.bio: Swiss businessman who took control of the Swiss watch industry group and put the Swatch at the centre of its recovery.

milestones.event: Took over the Swatch group.

people.name: Pierre Troisgros
people.bio: French chef of Roanne. With his brother Jean he ran the Frères Troisgros restaurant and made the salmon with sorrel sauce, a sauce that the cook did not thicken with flour. Some critics call him a father of nouvelle cuisine.

milestones.event: The Frères Troisgros restaurant in Roanne won its second Michelin star.
The restaurant won its third Michelin star.

people.name: Frank Gehry
people.bio: Canadian-American architect of sculptural forms clad in metal.

photo.credit: City of Toronto / Jose San Juan

milestones.event: Rebuilt his own house in Santa Monica with chain-link and corrugated metal.
Completed the Guggenheim Museum Bilbao.

people.name: Grace Kelly
people.bio: American actress and Princess of Monaco. A photograph of her with a structured Hermès bag in 1956 made the bag known by her name.

milestones.event: Held a Hermès handbag in front of her body in a magazine photograph; the maker renamed the bag the Kelly.

people.name: Henri Gault
people.bio: French food critic. With Christian Millau he started the restaurant guide Le Nouveau Guide in 1969. He used the phrase nouvelle cuisine for the new light cooking of the chefs of his time.

milestones.event: Started Le Nouveau Guide with Christian Millau.
Published with Millau the ten characteristics of nouvelle cuisine.

people.name: Jean-Luc Godard
people.bio: French-Swiss film director whose jump cuts broke the rules of film editing.

milestones.event: Released Breathless.
Released Pierrot le Fou.

people.name: Mary Quant
people.bio: British designer. Her boutique on the King's Road sold the miniskirt and the short shift to young London, and she made the street the source of the fashion.

milestones.event: Opened the boutique Bazaar on the King's Road, London.
Showed the Wet collection of PVC raincoats.
Received the OBE for services to fashion.

people.name: Steve McQueen
people.bio: American film actor and racing driver. He wore a square Heuer chronograph in the racing film Le Mans, and the model took his name in the market.

milestones.event: Wore a square Heuer Monaco chronograph in the film Le Mans.

people.name: Bernd Becher
people.bio: German photographer who, with Hilla Becher, made typologies of industrial buildings.

milestones.event: Showed in the New Topographics exhibition with Hilla Becher.

people.name: Denise Scott Brown
people.bio: Zambian-born American architect and planner who studied the commercial strip as architecture.

milestones.event: Published Learning from Las Vegas with Robert Venturi and Steven Izenour.

people.name: Gérald Genta
people.bio: Swiss watch designer. He drew the Royal Oak in 1972 and the Nautilus in 1976, the first steel sports watches with an integrated bracelet that cost as much as gold.

milestones.event: Drew the Royal Oak for Audemars Piguet, a steel watch with an octagonal bezel and eight screws.
Drew the Nautilus for Patek Philippe.

people.name: Dieter Rams
people.bio: German industrial designer of Braun products and the ten principles of good design.

milestones.event: Designed the SK 4 radio-phonograph with Hans Gugelot.
Designed the 606 universal shelving system on a grid of rails.
Became head of design at Braun.
Gave the talk that listed his principles of good design.

people.name: Eero Aarnio
people.bio: Finnish designer of the Ball chair and other fibreglass furniture in round forms.

milestones.event: Designed the Ball chair in fibreglass.

people.name: François Truffaut
people.bio: French critic and film director who attacked the old French cinema and then replaced it.

milestones.event: Published A Certain Tendency of the French Cinema.
Released The 400 Blows.

people.name: Michel Guérard
people.bio: French chef and pastry chef. He cooked at Asnières and at Eugénie-les-Bains, and made cuisine minceur for the guests of a spa. His restaurant Les Prés d'Eugénie held three Michelin stars from 1977.

milestones.event: Opened the restaurant Le Pot-au-Feu in Asnières-sur-Seine.
Moved to Eugénie-les-Bains and began his slimming cuisine for the spa guests.
Published La Grande Cuisine minceur; Time put him on its cover in February.
Les Prés d'Eugénie won its third Michelin star.

people.name: Richard Rogers
people.bio: British-Italian architect who put the services of a building on its outside.

milestones.event: Completed the Centre Pompidou in Paris with Renzo Piano.
Completed the Lloyd's building in London.

people.name: Giorgio Armani
people.bio: Italian designer. His soft, unstructured jackets in plain wool set the line of the working suit for both sexes in the 1980s.

milestones.event: Founded his fashion house in Milan with Sergio Galeotti.
Dressed the lead of the film American Gigolo in soft, unstructured jackets.

people.name: Hilla Becher
people.bio: German photographer who, with Bernd Becher, made typologies of industrial buildings.

milestones.event: Showed in the New Topographics exhibition with Bernd Becher.

people.name: Michael Graves
people.bio: American architect of colourful Postmodern buildings and household objects.

milestones.event: Completed the Portland Building in Oregon.
Designed the 9093 kettle with a bird whistle for Alessi.

people.name: Paco Rabanne
people.bio: Spanish-born French designer. He built dresses from plastic discs and metal rings, and so made metal and plastic a material of couture.

milestones.event: Showed 12 Unwearable Dresses in Contemporary Materials, made of plastic discs and metal links.

people.name: Mario Buatta
people.bio: American decorator called the Prince of Chintz, whose layered English country rooms are the source of the grandmillennial look.

people.name: Norman Foster
people.bio: English architect of High-tech buildings that show their structure and services.

milestones.event: Completed the HSBC Main Building in Hong Kong.
Won the Pritzker Architecture Prize.

people.name: Victor Moscoso
people.bio: Spanish-American artist of psychedelic posters with vibrating colour.

milestones.event: Made posters for the Family Dog and the Matrix in San Francisco.

people.name: Renzo Piano
people.bio: Italian architect who designed the Centre Pompidou with Richard Rogers.

photo.credit: Cirone-Musi (Festival della Scienza, Genova)Color and edits by the uploader.

milestones.event: Completed the Centre Pompidou in Paris.
Won the Pritzker Architecture Prize.

people.name: Robert Adams
people.bio: American photographer of the suburban American West.

milestones.event: Published The New West.
Showed in the New Topographics exhibition.

people.name: Wes Wilson
people.bio: American artist who made the psychedelic concert poster with melting letters.

milestones.event: Made the first of his Fillmore posters for Bill Graham.

people.name: Issey Miyake
people.bio: Japanese designer. He pressed polyester jersey into permanent pleats after the garment was cut, and so made clothes that are light and stretch.

milestones.event: Launched the Pleats Please line of heat-set pleated polyester.

people.name: Joel Meyerowitz
people.bio: American photographer who moved street photography into colour.

milestones.event: Published Cape Light.

people.name: Marcello Gandini
people.bio: Italian car designer. At Bertone he drew the low, flat wedge with a sharp crease that set the line of the supercar for 20 years.

milestones.event: Drew the Carabo show car for Bertone.
Drew the Stratos Zero show car, a wedge that was 84 cm high.
Showed the Countach prototype.

people.name: Terry de Havilland
people.bio: English shoemaker from a London shoe family. He made the bright platforms and wedges that glam rock musicians wore in the 1970s.

milestones.event: Made new three-tiered wedge shoes in snakeskin colours, from a pair that he found in his father's attic.
Became the rock and roll cobbler of the decade; his clients included David Bowie and Led Zeppelin.

people.name: Yvon Chouinard
people.bio: American climber and maker. He made climbing gear in California, and in 1973 he began to sell outdoor clothes. His firm helped to make polar fleece.

milestones.event: Began to sell outdoor clothes under the name Patagonia.
Worked with Malden Mills on a napped polyester pile that became polar fleece.

people.name: William Eggleston
people.bio: American photographer who made colour photography accepted as art.

milestones.event: Showed William Eggleston's Guide at MoMA.

people.name: Gunpei Yokoi
people.bio: Japanese engineer at Nintendo who designed the Game Boy around a cheap four-shade monochrome screen.

milestones.event: Led the design of the Game Boy and its four-shade screen.

people.name: Vivienne Westwood
people.bio: British designer. With Malcolm McLaren she made the torn, pinned, slogan-printed and bondage clothes that dressed the London punk scene.

milestones.event: Opened a shop at 430 King's Road, London, with Malcolm McLaren.
Renamed the shop SEX and sold rubber, leather and bondage clothes.

people.name: Calvin Klein
people.bio: American designer who founded a fashion house in 1968. In the 1980s his name on the waistband made plain underwear a branded and advertised product.

milestones.event: Launched the company that later took his name.
Put his name on the waistband of a plain brief and sold it as fashion.

people.name: Jeremiah Tower
people.bio: American chef. He was the chef of Chez Panisse from 1972 to 1978 and gave the daily menu its sharp, ripe and formal style. In 1984 he opened Stars in San Francisco.

milestones.event: Joined Chez Panisse as a cook and later as its chef.
Opened the restaurant Stars in San Francisco.

people.name: Rei Kawakubo
people.bio: Japanese designer. She founded Comme des Garçons and made black, loose, torn and lopsided clothes that questioned the shape of the body.

milestones.event: Founded the Comme des Garçons label in Tokyo.
Showed her first collection in Paris, in black, loose and torn clothes.
Showed Body Meets Dress, Dress Meets Body, with padded lumps on the body.

people.name: Jil Sander
people.bio: German designer. Her plain, fine and precisely cut clothes in neutral colours set the line of 1990s minimalism.

milestones.event: Opened her first boutique in Hamburg.

people.name: Yohji Yamamoto
people.bio: Japanese designer. His long, black, oversized clothes in wool and cotton set the dark, loose line of the Japanese wave in Paris.

milestones.event: Showed his first collection in Paris, in loose black clothes.

people.name: Alice Waters
people.bio: American chef, author and food activist. She opened Chez Panisse in Berkeley in 1971 and built the menu on fresh, seasonal produce from named local farms. She also began the Edible Schoolyard project in a Berkeley school.

milestones.event: Opened Chez Panisse in Berkeley.
Opened the Chez Panisse Café upstairs, with an à la carte menu.
Started the Chez Panisse Foundation and the Edible Schoolyard.

people.name: Dapper Dan
people.bio: American tailor of Harlem, New York. In the 1980s he printed luxury logos on leather and made jackets, bags and car seats for his clients.

milestones.event: Opened his boutique on 125th Street, Harlem.
By the mid-1980s printed luxury logos on leather with a silk-screen press.

people.name: Massimo Osti
people.bio: Italian designer of Bologna. He took sport and military cloth into dress, dyed whole garments and tried new fabrics for C.P. Company and Stone Island.

milestones.event: Launched Stone Island with a jacket of heavy rubberised cloth of the type used for truck covers.

people.name: Lewis Baltz
people.bio: American photographer of industrial parks and new tract houses.

milestones.event: Showed in the New Topographics exhibition.

people.name: Patrick Le Quément
people.bio: French designer. He led the design of Renault from 1987 and made small cars with soft, round forms and bright interiors.

milestones.event: Became director of design at Renault.
Showed the Twingo, a one-box city car with a round body.

people.name: Malcolm McLaren
people.bio: British impresario and shop owner. He ran the King's Road shop with Vivienne Westwood and managed the Sex Pistols, who wore its clothes.

milestones.event: Ran the SEX shop at 430 King's Road, London.
Became the manager of the Sex Pistols, and dressed the band in the shop's clothes.

people.name: Mark Perry
people.bio: English writer and musician who started the punk fanzine Sniffin' Glue.

Stopped the zine and formed the band Alternative TV.

people.name: Michel Bras
people.bio: French chef of Laguiole in the Aubrac, who built his menu from the wild and garden plants of the plateau and made the plate a small landscape.

milestones.event: Took over the kitchen of the family restaurant in Laguiole and began to cook from the plants of the plateau.
Made the first gargouillou, a dish of dozens of young vegetables, herbs and flowers.
Moved the restaurant to a new building on the Suquet plateau above Laguiole.

people.name: Axel Vervoordt
people.bio: Belgian art dealer and interior designer of rooms in raw, quiet materials.

people.name: Jamie Reid

Made the cover of Never Mind the Bollocks.

people.name: Stephen Shore
people.bio: American photographer of colour road trips across the United States.

people.name: Donna Karan

milestones.event: Showed Seven Easy Pieces, a system of work clothes for women.

people.name: Ed Logg
people.bio: American game designer at Atari who made arcade games for vector and raster screens.

milestones.event: Co-designed Asteroids, a vector-display arcade game.

people.name: John Pawson
people.bio: British architect who reduces a room to light, proportion and one material, with all storage hidden.

milestones.event: Completed the Calvin Klein flagship store on Madison Avenue, New York.
Published the book Minimum.

people.name: Nobu Matsuhisa
people.bio: Japanese chef who worked in Peru and Argentina before Los Angeles. He cooked Japanese fish with Peruvian chilli and citrus and opened Matsuhisa in 1987 and Nobu in New York in 1994.

milestones.event: Opened the restaurant Matsuhisa in Los Angeles.
Opened the first Nobu in New York with Robert De Niro and partners.

people.name: Wolfgang Puck
people.bio: Austrian-American chef trained in France. He opened Spago in Los Angeles in 1982 and Chinois on Main in Santa Monica in 1983, where he put Chinese flavours on a French and Californian plate.

milestones.event: Opened Spago on the Sunset Strip in Los Angeles.
Opened Chinois on Main in Santa Monica.

people.name: Ken Kutaragi
people.bio: Japanese engineer at Sony who led the design of the PlayStation and its polygon hardware.

milestones.event: Led the launch of the PlayStation in Japan.

people.name: Zaha Hadid

milestones.event: Showed her work in the Deconstructivist Architecture show at MoMA.

Won the Pritzker Architecture Prize.

people.name: Dave Theurer
people.bio: American game designer at Atari who made colour vector arcade games with deep perspective.

milestones.event: Designed Tempest, a colour vector game seen down a tube in perspective.

Designed the Tolomeo lamp with Giancarlo Fassina.

people.name: Elmar Mock

people.name: Nan Goldin
people.bio: American photographer of her own circle at night, lit by direct flash.

people.name: J Mays

people.name: David Carson
people.bio: American graphic designer of layered, broken magazine type.

Joined the chefs who gave Hawaii regional cuisine its name.

people.name: Nathalie Du Pasquier

people.bio: German photographer of raw, flash-lit fashion pictures.

people.name: Stefan Sonnenfeld
people.bio: American colourist who graded blockbusters in teal and orange.

milestones.event: Graded Transformers.

people.name: Kazuko Shibuya

people.bio: American film director whose action films made the teal and orange grade common.

people.name: Robyn Miller

Led the design team that released the Apple Watch.
Left Apple and founded LoveFrom.

people.name: Franz von Holzhausen

people.name: Cliff Bleszinski
